newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom completes latest shr buyback phase.
newsitem.headline: Telecom completes latest shr buyback phase.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand said on Monday it had concluded the lastest phase of its NZ$1 billion buyback programme and spent a total of NZ$227 million on 32.45 million shares to add to its purchases totalling 54.73 million shares made in the first phase earlier in the year.
The last purchases were made on Friday last week.
This concluded the second tranche of a programme conceived to be in four parts, and finance manager Pat Duignan said in a statement that the operation was on track.
"We are more than half way (through) and expect to complete the repurchase plan in two more tranches. We have acquired 61.4 percent of our on-market target," he added.

As well as on-market purchases, Telecom is also buying stock direct at market prices from major shareholders Bell Atlantic and Ameritech in order for them to remain below their legally mandated 24.95 percent shareholding limit.
To date the company has repurchased 4.6 percent of its total issued capital and as a side effect of the plan its weighting in the NZSE-40 Capital Index has dipped to 25.41 percent.
On a bullish day for the stock market, Telecom shares closed up a massive 20 cents at NZ$7.50.
The company said this move indicated price support had come from other buyers even when it was no longer in the market itself.
